collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A child asks an elder what happens after people die: admit not knowing, or tell the stories people believe.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been very quiet since the funeral. Tonight (subject.he/she) asks (friend), who is the oldest person (subject.he/she) knows, what happens after people die. (friend) has wondered the same thing for seventy years. What should (friend) say?

text_only.reason: a death only talked about (or the word's everyday sense); nobody dies -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) says (friend.he/she) does not know, and neither does anyone else, not for sure. (subject) is surprised that grown-ups do not know everything. Then (subject.he/she) seems relieved. "So I can wonder too?" (subject.he/she) asks. (friend) says yes, that is allowed.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) tells (subject) the different things people on Isola believe: that the dead rest, that they go on somewhere, that they come back as birds, that they live on in the people who remember them. (subject) decides (subject.he/she) likes the bird one best, and watches the birds very carefully after that.
